songs.name: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Tight set highlighted by Good Lovin’, Midnight Hour & Hurts Me Too
ai_show_review.blurb: The band delivers strong renditions of Good Lovin’, In the Midnight Hour and a fiery It Hurts Me Too. Pigpen’s vocal fire powers the second half while Jerry’s guitar shines on China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider. The Miller soundboard capture is crisp with only a tiny tape cut‑off at the very end.
ai_show_review.review: December 27, 1970 at Legion Stadium finds the Dead in top‑form, rolling through two solid sets that balance relaxed storytelling with high‑energy rock. Jerry Garcia rip‑throughs Good Lovin’ and lays down an expressive solo on China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, while his vocal harmonies sparkle throughout. Pigpen steals the spotlight with a gritty intro on In the Midnight Hour, a shouted “No you don’t” before Turn On Your Lovelight, and a soulful, slightly flubbed delivery that keeps the crowd laughing. Phil Lesh anchors the groove with solid bass lines and surprising country‑flavored leads on Cumberland Blues, and Bob Weir’s rhythm tone shines especially on China Cat Sunflower > Rider. The set builds nicely—first half feels laid‑back, second half erupts with Hurts Me Too, Attics Of My Life and a seamless Not Fade Away → Goin’ Down The Road Feeling Bad medley. The Miller soundboard recording captures the performance with crisp clarity, only a faint hiss and a minor cut‑off at the tape’s end, making it the definitive listening source for this classic early‑70s show.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture – crisp, raw mix with minimal hiss and only a tiny end‑tape cut‑off, presenting the full set in clear detail.

song_highlights: Going Down The Road Feeling Bad

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is front‑and‑center – ripping riffs on Good Lovin’, expressive solo on China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, and a standout vocal harmony throughout, especially on Hurts Me Too.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a solid bass foundation and top‑form backing vocals; his country‑flavored lead on Cumberland Blues adds an unexpected highlight.
band_performance.Bob: Weir delivers a bright rhythm tone (notably on China Cat Sunflower > Rider) and a double‑shot vocal on Mama Tried, fueling the energy of Good Lovin’ and Sugar Magnolia.
band_performance.Pigpen: Ron “Pigpen” McKernan brings spirited vocal introductions, playful lyric flubs that engage the crowd, and a fiery shout before Lovelight, driving the show’s second half.
